request.text:
The Sheffer stroke (NAND) and Peirce arrow (NOR) are each functionally
complete for positive arities.  Neither represents a nullary truth
function: a formula built from NAND or NOR alone always contains a
variable, so the two constants need separately declared constants such as
\(\bottom\) and \(\topv\)
(\cref{thm:p01-w02-p01-024-nand-nor,thm:p01-w02-p01-024-no-closed}).

\section{Binding and precedence}
\label{sec:p01-binding-precedence}
\index{precedence}\index{binding}

The grammar declared by the active language is always primary.  After unique
readability has been established, Table~\ref{tab:p01-precedence} licenses the
parentheses omitted in expository formulas.  Smaller numerical ranks bind
more tightly.  Operators sharing a rank are governed by the association
column; unrelated subsystem symbols share a rank only where their scopes are
disjoint.

Typeface alone never assigns standing.  Table~\ref{tab:p01-letter-families}
counts, for each letter family, the register rows whose glyph uses it and
the distinct scopes those rows record; it is generated from
\texttt{registry/symbols.csv}, and the generated master register above
remains authoritative for each individual symbol, role and scope.

\input{generated/symbols-letter-families}

The family-level defaults are these.  Greek lowercase \(\varphi,\psi,\chi\)
and \(\sigma,\tau\) are the global formula and sentence metavariables; Greek
uppercase \(\Gamma,\Delta,\Sigma,\Pi\) are global formula contexts;
calligraphic \(\mathcal L\) and \(\mathcal M,\mathcal N\) are the global
signature and structure metavariables; blackboard \(\mathbb N\) is the
global natural-number set.  No Fraktur glyph has a global row: each Fraktur
glyph in the register is confined to the scope its own row records, and a
further use requires a scoped row before substantive use.  Roman and
sans-serif names denote named operations and fixed systems or operators,
never generic variables.  Any other letter receives a role only through its
own scoped row.
